The Arabic release passed translation review: every string comes from the ARB files and reads well. On the first Arabic test build, the screens still run left to right. After someone adds

to the app, most of it flips, but the order list doesn't look right. The 16-pixel gap now sits next to the arrow instead of where the Arabic text starts, the titles hug the wrong edge, the discount badge is stuck in the top-left corner, and every row's arrow points back into the text.
The belief: supporting Arabic means translating the strings. Flutter handles RTL, so once the text is Arabic, the layout will sort itself out.

Icons flip only if they're marked
mirrors in RTL only when its

, which looks almost the same, doesn't. That flag matches Apple's guidance: "Flip an interface icon that shows forward or backward motion", so "a back button must point to the right" in RTL. But "Don't flip logos or universal signs and marks", a clock stays a clock, and you should "avoid flipping images like photographs".

Two more rules from Apple are easy to miss. "Don't reverse the order of numerals in a specific number": an order number reads the same in both directions. And "Align a paragraph based on its language, not on the current context", where a paragraph means three or more lines. An English review shown in the Arabic UI is hard to read when it's aligned to the right.

content.text: In a widget test on an 800-pixel-wide screen set to RTL, the

flipped both versions: the icon moved to the left end. But the wrong row kept 16 pixels on the left, next to the icon, and only 8 on the right, where Arabic text starts. Its title hugged the left edge of its space, and the arrow still pointed right, back into the text. The right row had 16 pixels on the right, a right-aligned title and a mirrored chevron. In LTR, the two rows were pixel-identical, which is why this bug survives every review done in English.
